clue.text: Board bringing in a head ready to educate

definitions.note: read as ready for someone to educate, i.e. open to being taught

indicators.note: bringing in says the board takes the other piece inside itself

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board
a head means apiece or each, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A school board takes on a head teacher keen to start educating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' puts EACH inside TABLE, after its T. The definition is loose: it means ready for educating, not ready to do the educating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receptive to instruction can readily be taught.

clue.text: King finally leaves to speak for all

indicators.note: finally leaves says the king's letter departs from the very end of the phrase

parts.note: to speak is to talk
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch at last departs, leaving others to speak for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally leaves' removes the K from the end of TO TALK.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole sum or entirety is the total.

clue.text: Penalty varied in quantity

indicators.note: varied means the letters of penalty are changed about

explanation.surface: A penalty that changes, depending on the amount involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges PENALTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentifully, in abundance, is an adverbial sense of in quantity.

clue.text: With two of hearts, battle to produce trick after this?

indicators.note: two of here asks for the opening pair of letters of the word hearts

parts.note: Ypres was the site of First World War battles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Using a pair of hearts, a card player fights to pull off a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two of' takes HE from hearts. YPRES is a Belgian town famous for three First World War battles.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjuror's exclamation is said as a trick is completed.

clue.text: Tolerant description of travellers, proverbially

parts.note: the proverb says travel broadens the mind, so travellers are given wider minds

explanation.surface: How the saying characterises those who travel: open-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerant people are liberal and open in outlook.

clue.text: Centre of 24 needs backing in decline

indicators.note: needs backing says the middle letters are read backwards
centre of asks for the middle letters of that word

parts.note: the answer to 24 across is RUBBERS

explanation.surface: The middle of a team needs support as it falters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of' takes BBE from the middle of RUBBERS; 'needs backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to recede or dwindle, like a falling tide.

clue.text: Vestment old peasant hasn't finished

indicators.note: hasn't finished says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cottar was a Scottish peasant tenant of former times

explanation.surface: A garment an old peasant never got round to completing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' drops the last letter, R, from COTTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A short surplice worn by clergy and choristers is a cotta.

clue.text: Gorge that's deep, as a rule

definitions.meaning: a deep ravine; the Spanish spelling of canyon
a principle or standard, as in church law

explanation.surface: A deep ravine, as a general principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Canyon has a Spanish spelling, cañon, while a canon is a law or standard.

clue.text: Ram cart with back to front vehicle

indicators.note: back to front here means the last letter of the phrase is moved to the start

explanation.surface: A battering ram on a cart, its rear turned forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with back to front' moves the T at the end of RAMCART to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram carriage is a type of road vehicle running on rails.

clue.text: Arranging to have one kind of product imported, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: one kind of product is a line, a range of goods; imported means meant, signified

explanation.surface: Organising a particular range of goods to be brought in from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A LINE (a product range) plus MEANT (imported, as in signified), heard together, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting things in order or in a straight row is alignment.

clue.text: Coach's shout to encourage pack

definitions.meaning: the name of a famous nineteenth-century London stagecoach
the huntsman's cry urging hounds on after sighting a fox

explanation.surface: A sports trainer yells to spur on the forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho was both a stagecoach name and the hunting halloo to the hounds.

clue.text: Asian language or English used in Oriental island

indicators.note: used in says the English goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: Which tongue is spoken in an Eastern island: native or English?
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts ENG inside BALI, after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of Bangladesh and West Bengal is Bengali.

clue.text: Vessel from Silesia?

parts.note: Silesia is also a twilled cotton fabric used for linings, so something made from it would line a garment

explanation.surface: A ship from a region of central Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Silesia looks like the Polish region, but it is a cloth used to line pockets and garments.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean-going passenger ship, or a lining, is a liner.

clue.text: There's a place in the order for this West Indian

definitions.text: There's a place in the order for this West Indian

parts.words: There's a place in the order for this West Indian
parts.note: a native of the island of Dominica shares a name with a member of the Order of Preachers founded by St Dominic

explanation.surface: A man from the Caribbean has a spot reserved for him in a religious brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a Black Friar and someone from Dominica or the Dominican Republic carry this name.

clue.text: Popular player eliminated? Nothing odd there

indicators.note: odd means the letters are turned into a strange new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A star performer is knocked out of a contest; nothing strange about that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ELIMINATED plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome actor adored by afternoon theatre audiences is a heart-throb of the stage.

clue.text: Centres in countries for playing sport

indicators.note: centres in asks for the middle letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Midfielders in national teams line up to play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centres in' takes T, O and Y, the middle letters of countries, for and playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport or trifle with something is to play idly with it.

clue.text: Visible records of alternating current's limits

parts.note: the sea's ebbing and flowing water is a current that alternates
marks are limits, as in boundary marks

explanation.surface: Measurements showing the peaks of AC in an electrical circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternating current' looks electrical; here it is the sea, coming in and going out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines left on a shore or bath show where water reached.

clue.text: Red Cross hero goes tearing off

indicators.note: off means the letters are disordered, as food that has gone off

explanation.surface: A humanitarian aid worker rushes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges GOES TEARING. England's flag is the red cross of its patron saint, the dragon-slayer.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint's emblem is a red cross on white.

clue.text: Regard -vestige as part of cosmetic exercise?

parts.note: to regard something is to eye it
a shadow is a trace or vestige

explanation.surface: Looking upon a remnant as one element of a beauty routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured powder for the lids is part of a make-up session.

clue.text: Runs one musical entertainment after another? That sounds terrible

parts.note: a disco is a dance party with recorded music
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
another musical entertainment is a dance

explanation.surface: An organiser stages one musical show after another; the noise is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The R for runs sits between the two entertainments, DISCO first, then DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh, clashing noise lacks harmony.

clue.text: It takes grit to seize this weapon

parts.note: grit is sand
to bag is to seize or capture

explanation.surface: You need courage to grab hold of this arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grit' looks like courage; it is sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand-filled cosh is a bludgeon used as a weapon.

clue.text: Queen, possibly, allowed to see king

definitions.meaning: a queen is a female of a certain household pet
the proverb says a ... may look at a king

explanation.surface: Perhaps the queen is permitted an audience with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A female feline is a queen, and the proverb permits one to gaze at royalty.

clue.text: Warn an amusing fellow

definitions.meaning: to admonish or advise of danger
a droll or mischievous person, as in he's a real one

explanation.surface: Tell off a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution is to give a warning, and a caution is old slang for an entertaining character.

clue.text: Roughly treat Germans — writer and composer, say

indicators.note: say means these names are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Thomas Mann, the German novelist, and Handel, the German-born composer

explanation.surface: Two German artists, a novelist and a musician, are subjected to rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: MANN plus HANDEL, spoken together, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle someone roughly and forcefully is to manhandle them.

clue.text: Spy's book featured in a Times leader

indicators.note: featured in says one piece is set within the other
leader asks for the first letter of Times

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for Genesis, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A secret agent's memoir is promoted in a newspaper editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' puts GEN inside A and T, the 'leader' of Times.
explanation.definitionFit: An undercover operative working for a government is an agent.

clue.text: Hard relative to visit, lately?

definitions.note: a ghost of the recently deceased, the late, visits the living

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A difficult relation who has come to stay recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lately' hints that the visitor is late, i.e. dead: a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts frequent the places they knew, returning in spirit.

clue.text: As part of gift, it helps

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being included in a present is useful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'As' covers the whole clue's sense: a tithe is a gift to the church, and it helps.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is weak; a tithe is a tenth of produce given to the church, a kind of gift.

clue.text: Footwear used by Americans in lots of games

definitions.meaning: in the US, overshoes or galoshes
a series of games in bridge or whist, best of three

explanation.surface: Shoes worn by Americans for many sporting contests.
explanation.definitionFit: American overshoes and card-game series both carry this name.

clue.text: Main cause of poet's fever

definitions.meaning: the main is an old word for the ocean
John Masefield's poem ... Fever begins I must go down to the ... again

explanation.surface: The chief reason a poet falls ill.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is the main, and it gave Masefield his fever.

clue.text: Exponent of an earlier genre, not pop art

definitions.text: Exponent of an earlier genre, not pop art

parts.words: Exponent of an earlier genre, not pop art
parts.note: an artist of the anti-art movement of around 1916 that preceded pop art

explanation.surface: A practitioner of an older style rather than modern pop art.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Zurich anti-art movement of the First World War years.

clue.text: Spot a great deal

definitions.meaning: to see or catch a glimpse of
a lot, as in a ... better

explanation.surface: Notice a real bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to catch a glimpse, and a sight more means far more.

clue.text: Money given regularly for admission

definitions.meaning: pocket money or a regular payment

explanation.surface: Cash handed over periodically to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket money is an allowance, as is a concession granted.
